extraction.name: Prompted Textures Dataset (PTD)
extraction.description: A high-quality, diverse texture dataset of 246,285 images across 56 texture classes, generated using text-to-image models and refined through a multi-stage process to ensure quality, diversity, and alignment with prompts. The dataset is designed to support texture-based research, including interpretability, bias analysis, and robustness in machine learning models.
extraction.creator: Blaine Hoak, Patrick McDaniel
extraction.citeAs: Hoak, B., & McDaniel, P. (2025). On Synthetic Texture Datasets: Challenges, Creation, and Curation. arXiv:2409.10297.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was generated using a three-step methodology: (1) creating texture-specific prompts by combining artistically-informed descriptors across texture classes, (2) using Stable Diffusion model pipelines to generate texture images from these prompts, and (3) applying a three-stage refinement process (frequency filtering, patch variance filtering, and CLIP scoring) to enhance quality and alignment with prompts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data was generated using the Stable Diffusion model from HuggingFace, with prompts constructed from combinations of descriptors (texture type, artistic style, spatial arrangement, color, and enhancers) to ensure controlled diversity.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset underwent a three-stage refinement process: (1) frequency filtering to remove object-like images by analyzing Fourier transforms, (2) patch variance filtering to eliminate homogeneous images by dividing images into 50x50 patches and computing variance, and (3) CLIP score filtering to retain images with the highest alignment to prompts.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The preprocessing involved generating 5 images per prompt using Stable Diffusion, followed by a multi-stage refinement process to filter out low-quality or misaligned images. The refinement steps included frequency filtering, patch variance filtering, and CLIP scoring to ensure high-quality, diverse, and representative textures.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset was annotated through the generation process itself, where prompts were used to create texture images. Human evaluations were conducted to assess quality and representativeness, with participants rating images on a scale of 1 to 5 for overall quality and alignment with descriptors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Human evaluations were conducted using a custom interface where participants rated images on quality and representativeness. The Stable Diffusion model and CLIP scoring were used for automated filtering and alignment checks.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human evaluations confirmed that each stage of the refinement process improved dataset quality, with a 3.4% increase in quality and a 4.5% increase in representativeness. CLIP scores were used to validate human assessments, showing strong alignment between automated and human evaluations.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 9 participants were recruited for human evaluation, with each evaluating 100 images. Demographics were not explicitly detailed in the paper.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stable Diffusion, CLIP scoring, Fourier transforms, patch variance analysis
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is available for download on Zenodo (https://zenodo.org/records/15359142) and has been used as a basis for further research, including the development of the Texture Object Association Values (TAV) metric. The authors note that the dataset has reached 23 downloads at the time of submission.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables advancements in texture-based research, including interpretability, bias analysis, and robustness in machine learning models. It has been used to measure texture bias in models, uncovering associations between textures and objects that affect model predictions.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset generation process encountered biases in the Stable Diffusion safety filter, which flagged benign texture images as NSFW (e.g., textures like 'paisley' were frequently flagged). This highlights the need for refined NSFW filters that can better handle abstract or texture-based content.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset may have limitations in generating highly structured textures (e.g., 'grid' or 'polka-dotted') compared to more complex textures (e.g., 'hairy' or 'flaky'). Additionally, the refinement process may exclude some valid textures due to strict filtering criteria.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The dataset is designed for texture-based research, including interpretability, bias analysis, and robustness in machine learning models. It has been used to measure texture bias and uncover texture-object associations in models.
